quarterly_data.signal: The FDA granted accelerated approval (June 13, 2026) to Tzield to delay the decline in endogenous insulin production in children aged eight to 17 recently diagnosed with stage 3 type 1 diabetes, which Sanofi calls the first disease-modifying therapy for these patients. The approval rests on the PROTECT phase 3 study (328 children and adolescents randomized 2:1, Tzield n=217 vs placebo n=111), which significantly slowed the decrease in mean C-peptide versus placebo (difference in least-squares means 0.13 pmol/mL; 95% CI 0.09-0.17; p<0.001), plus program data from over 900 patients; continued approval may be contingent upon verification of clinical benefit in confirmatory study(ies), and the confirmatory BETA-PRESERVE phase 3 study has been initiated and is enrolling. Tzield's stage 2 indication is also approved in the UK, the EU (Teizeild), China, Australia, Canada, Israel, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Kuwait, Brazil and Switzerland.
